title: Sell Mineral Rights in Silesia, MT
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Silesia, MT
metaDescription: Silesia, MT was named for Polish-Silesian coal miners and sits near the Elk Basin oil field. I buy mineral interests here based on actual recorded title.
heroLead: Silesia was named by the coal miners who settled it, and it sits close enough to the Elk Basin field that both mineral histories run through this stretch of Carbon County.
intro: The name tells you the origin — Silesia was a coal camp settled largely by miners from the Silesia region of central Europe, working the same coal belt that ran through Red Lodge and Bridger. What makes this particular spot on the map different is proximity to Elk Basin, one of the oldest oil fields in the northern Rockies, discovered in 1915 and still producing at low stripper rates over a century later along the Montana-Wyoming line. A family mineral interest near Silesia can plausibly touch either history, or both.

That double history is exactly why I don't shortcut the title work here. Two Silesia-area parcels a half-mile apart can carry completely different mineral pictures depending on which era the original severance dates to.

sections.heading: Elk Basin's long, slow decline
paragraphs: Elk Basin has been producing for more than a hundred years, which sounds impressive until you understand what stripper-well decline actually looks like this late in a field's life — low, steady volumes, thin margins for the operator, and royalty checks that reflect that reality rather than boom-era numbers. If your interest touches this field, I evaluate it against current decline curves, not against what an old family story says it was worth decades ago.

sections.heading: Coal-era severances layered underneath
paragraphs: Because this ground was coal country before it was oil country, I check whether your deed reserved coal rights, oil and gas rights, or both, and whether those rights were later split apart in a separate conveyance. It's a common enough pattern here that I never assume.

faqs.question: Does my interest near Silesia touch the Elk Basin field?
faqs.answer: Possibly — it depends on your exact legal description. I check that against the field's current boundary and any active units before quoting.

faqs.question: Elk Basin has been producing since 1915 — is my interest worth a lot?
faqs.answer: Age doesn't equal value this late in a field's life. Elk Basin is in long stripper-well decline, and I price interests against current production, not the field's history.

faqs.question: Could my family's deed be coal rights instead of oil and gas?
faqs.answer: It's possible given the area's coal-camp history. I read the actual deed language to confirm what you hold before making an offer.

faqs.question: Who holds the county records for a Silesia-area parcel?
faqs.answer: The Carbon County Clerk and Recorder in Red Lodge. I pull the chain directly rather than relying on family recollection of the original severance.
